claims.text: Binder jetting forms a binder-containing green body from metal powder at ambient temperature.
The binder-jetted green body is subsequently densified using an isothermal sintering step.
Appropriately selected sintering temperature and time can provide full or sufficient inter-diffusion between powder particles.
Binder jetting followed by isothermal sintering will produce a more homogeneous AlCrFeNiSi microstructure than melting-based fabrication.
Binder jetting followed by isothermal sintering will reduce segregation in AlCrFeNiSi relative to melting-based fabrication.
Binder jetting followed by isothermal sintering will lower residual stress in AlCrFeNiSi relative to melting-based fabrication.
Binder jetting followed by isothermal sintering will decrease defect density in AlCrFeNiSi.
The isothermal sintering process enables solid-state diffusion between AlCrFeNiSi particles.
Binder jetting and isothermal sintering avoid the rapid cooling and melt-pool dynamics characteristic of melting-based additive manufacturing.
Eliminating significant thermal gradients during processing prevents the development of residual thermal stresses.
Full inter-diffusion and isothermal processing prevent compositional gradients.
Avoiding compositional gradients and residual thermal stresses reduces defect formation.
Reduced segregation, residual stress, and defect density improve the overall mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi.
Binder-jetted and sintered AlCrFeNiSi will have increased microhardness relative to melt-processed AlCrFeNiSi.
Binder-jetted and sintered AlCrFeNiSi will have improved ductility relative to melt-processed AlCrFeNiSi.
Binder-jetted and sintered AlCrFeNiSi will have increased tensile strength relative to melt-processed AlCrFeNiSi.
Conventionally melt-processed AlCrFeNiSi has significant segregation and defect formation associated with rapid cooling.
Conventionally melt-processed AlCrFeNiSi has significant residual stresses associated with thermal gradients.
Excessive sintering temperature or time could trigger grain growth and compromise the expected improvements.
Changes in powder-feedstock characteristics could compromise the expected benefits of binder jetting and isothermal sintering.
